data.summary: The pod startup was slow due to an extremely long image pull. The 53 MB image took 56.5 seconds to pull because the throughput from the registry was very low, at approximately 0.9 MB/s. This significantly exceeded the 10.0-second SLO.

findings.statement: The total pod startup time was 57.0 seconds, which breached the SLO threshold of 10.0 seconds.
The image pull phase was the dominant factor, taking 56.488 seconds of the total startup time.
The image size was 53328919 bytes (approximately 53 MB).
The image pull throughput was very low at 944075 bytes/s (approximately 0.9 MB/s), which is below the expected threshold of 5 MB/s.

ruled_out.reason: While the image is 53 MB, the primary issue is the extremely low pull throughput of 0.9 MB/s, not the image size itself being inherently large for normal throughput.
There was no time spent on model loading, with 'model_s' reported as 0.0 seconds.
Application initialisation ('app_init') was very fast, taking only 0.909 seconds.
The pod did not experience any scheduling delays, with 'scheduling_s' reported as 0.0 seconds and no failed scheduling events.
The readiness probe was instantaneous, taking 0.0 seconds, and there were no dependency connection delays.

recommendations.rationale: The primary cause of the slow startup is the low image pull throughput. Improving the network path to the registry or using a faster registry will reduce image pull times.
For cold starts, caching images on worker nodes can significantly reduce pull times by avoiding repeated downloads from the registry.
